text: Octopuses have three hearts.
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not.
Sharks have been around for longer than trees have.
Wombat poo is shaped like little cubes.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
Lightning is several times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The Eiffel Tower can grow about 15 centimetres taller in hot weather, because metal expands when it warms up.
Sea otters sometimes hold hands while they sleep so they do not drift apart.
Babies are born with around 300 bones. Grown-ups have 206, because some of them join together.
The Sun is about 109 times wider than the Earth.
Butterflies taste with their feet.
A polar bear's fur looks white, but its skin is black.
There are hundreds of different pasta shapes.
Potatoes were first grown in the Andes mountains in South America, thousands of years ago.
A tomato is a fruit, even though we cook it like a vegetable.
Instant noodles were invented in Japan in 1958.
The very first Christmas card was sent in London in 1843.
Dolphins sleep with half of their brain awake.
A giraffe has seven neck bones, the same number as you.
Cats have about 32 tiny muscles in each ear.
A rainbow is really a full circle. From the ground you only see the top part.
Some penguins give their partner a pebble as a present.
Sloths can hold their breath for longer than dolphins can.
Jupiter has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot that has been going for hundreds of years.
A snail has thousands of tiny teeth on its tongue.
Honeybees beat their wings about 200 times every second.
Honey can last for thousands of years without going off.
Cows have best friends and can get upset when they are split up.
Mount Everest grows a few millimetres taller every year.
No two tigers have the same stripes, just like no two people have the same fingerprints.
A tiger's stripes are on its skin too, not just its fur.
Tigers are the biggest of all the wild cats, and unlike most cats they love to swim.
Pugs were first bred in China, hundreds of years ago, as pets for important families.
A group of pugs is called a grumble.
The pug's old motto means "a lot in a little".
Super Mario first appeared in 1981 in a game called Donkey Kong, where he was called Jumpman.
Tetris was made in 1984 by a computer programmer called Alexey Pajitnov.
Pong, one of the first video games anyone could play at home or in an arcade, came out in 1972.
The modern circus began in London in 1768, with a horse rider called Philip Astley.
People have been juggling for thousands of years: there is an ancient Egyptian painting of jugglers that is about 4,000 years old.
Spaghetti means "little strings" in Italian.
Penne is named after pen nibs, because of its pointy, slanted ends.
World Pasta Day is on the 25th of October.
A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.
Footprints on the Moon will stay there for a very long time, because there is no wind or rain to wash them away.
Saturn is so light for its size that it would float if you could find a bathtub big enough.
More than a million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach us.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from the Earth, by about 4 centimetres every year.
Astronauts get a little taller in space, because there is no gravity pressing them down.
Mars looks red because its dust is full of rusty iron.
Space is silent, because there is no air for sound to travel through.
